name: trap
entries: A pressure tile seals both doors and slowly fills the room with harmless fog hiding the actual pit.
A rune swaps the voices of the first two creatures crossing it until they sincerely agree on something.
A treasure chest loudly accuses whoever opens it of theft, alerting nearby guardians by name.
A hallway repeats itself until travelers walk backward or extinguish every light.
A tripwire releases dozens of glass marbles while hidden shutters create a steep downhill floor.
A door handle steals the opener's shadow; the shadow runs ahead to warn enemies and exaggerate the party's strength.
A false healing fountain restores armor while quietly transferring equal damage to the next person who drinks.
A ceiling rune reverses gravity for loose objects first, providing a brief warning before affecting creatures.
A jeweled idol teleports into the pack of whoever touches it while replacing itself with a screaming replica.
A stairway counts spoken numbers; saying thirteen animates the steps into a stone serpent.
A locked gate opens easily when pushed but triggers darts when lockpicks enter the decorative keyhole.
A mirror creates one hostile reflection per visible weapon; covering or dropping weapons prevents new copies.
A floor of enchanted coins grips metal boots and armor while a rolling stone approaches very slowly.
A painted eye marks the first person who lies nearby, causing every statue ahead to watch and target them.
A bridge becomes intangible when anyone runs, forcing the group to cross calmly despite an approaching threat.
A music box puts listeners to sleep only when its melody stops, making destroying it immediately dangerous.
A pantry mimic is harmless, but attacking it awakens the entire hungry kitchen.
A rune of silence suppresses all sound while bells hidden on intruders still alert guards elsewhere.
An ornate rug rolls around trespassers, then politely asks for a password while dragging them toward a chute.
A trapped book erases one common word from the reader's vocabulary and uses the stolen word as its command phrase.
A corridor fills with illusory fire that causes no harm unless someone tries to extinguish it.
A statue offers safe passage for one honest compliment; flattery or sarcasm releases stone wasps.
A chest contains genuine treasure balanced over a mechanism triggered only when too much weight is removed.
A door teleports anyone opening it to the opposite side but leaves their carried equipment behind.
A frost rune freezes the brightest object in the room, encouraging clever control of light.
A harmless dart marks its target with a scent that attracts the dungeon's real predator.
A circular chamber rotates its exits whenever someone mentions a destination.
A golden rope can be crossed safely but tightens around anyone attempting to cut or step over it.
A guardian portrait asks a personal question; refusing locks the door, while lying releases the subject of the lie.
A pedestal grants the requested object, then announces an inconvenient but fair price that must be paid before leaving.
